A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TTOM work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional appendices in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTOM evaluations on T2V-CompBench and VBench, attention-layout probing, quantitative ablations, and qualitative generation results, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative experiments examining memory, optimization, retrieval rank, complex trajectories, and failures.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same layout planning, JSD attention-to-layout objective, LoRA optimization, and parametric memory operations. Appendix C documents planning prompts without establishing a changed implementation; Appendix D adds theoretical analysis.

E1.justification: The two benchmarks and GPT-4o-generated memory prompts remain unchanged. Figure 9 extends the explicitly reported test scenarios with a staged nonlinear trajectory: a cat moves upward and then toward the lower right. This is a limited extension within compositional video generation.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–10 are unchanged, including LVD and CogVideoX-5B with DyST-XL. New qualitative figures reuse Wan2.1-14B and TTOM component variants without introducing another baseline method.

E3.justification: Figure 8 adds a qualitative comparison using memory entries at retrieval ranks 1, 3, and 5, distinct from Table 4's retained average-fusion Top-k experiment. Existing benchmark metrics, memory-freezing policy, backbone configurations, and optimization settings remain unchanged. Appendix C supplies newly disclosed planning settings.

E4.justification: Figures 7–10 add qualitative component ablations, a retrieval-rank sensitivity example, complex-motion cases, and explicit failures. These provide bounded diagnostic evidence alongside the unchanged quantitative ablations in Tables 3–8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new qualitative experiments do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All ten tables and the attention-layout probe retain their numerical results, including Table 1's TTOM averages of 0.5632 and 0.6155. Figures 7–10 add qualitative findings about memory/TTO benefits, retrieval sensitivity, complex trajectories, and numeracy/motion failures.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces a task-to-optimal-parameter formulation, task-parameter smoothness and local strong-convexity assumptions, a gradient-descent convergence bound, a retrieval-initialization rule, and a storage-based forgetting argument in Equations 4–7. v1 has method definitions and objectives but no comparable formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract changes TTOM's characterization from 'training-free' to 'model-agnostic,' explicitly foregrounding model independence. The principal optimization/memory contributions and empirical effectiveness, transferability, and generalization claims remain unchanged; the conclusion still calls TTOM training-free.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the interpretation of memory through manifold-aware initialization, accelerated convergence, claimed immunity to catastrophic forgetting, and approximately optimal retention. Figure 7 additionally explains weak dynamics through small-amplitude planned layouts, while Figure 10 explicitly acknowledges failures. These go beyond v1's existing initialization and efficiency discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information with prompts for enrichment, metadata extraction, layout generation, and separate verification stages, including six-frame planning, 720×480 coordinates, object IDs, and consistency rules. The new Reproducibility Statement identifies the already-present project link as code access; it does not establish a newly available release.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning compositional generation and planning, retrieval, and personalization, including SILMM, TIGER, and Vincie. The related-work organization and positioning against per-sample layout control and existing TTT memory mechanisms remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes the repeated 'In this paradigm' phrase and duplicated streaming-setting paragraph, makes small terminology and typographical edits, and updates publication and author formatting. It adds a Reproducibility Statement and Appendices C–D while retaining the main narrative and section order.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to reorganize planning, denoising, memory, and gradient pathways. Figures 7–10 expand the visual presentation with component comparisons, retrieval patterns, trajectory layouts, and failures; Appendix C adds boxed prompt listings. Existing tables and other original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The planning prompts, clearer overview, and diagnostic and failure examples improve reproducibility and transparency while preserving the original quantitative evidence. The gain is tempered by Appendix D: its convergence argument is conditional, and its forgetting-immunity claim assumes unchanged stored entries despite Section 3.3 allowing matched entries to be updated. The documentation gains support a limited overall improvement, rather than stronger validated performance or guarantees.
